Soft pneumatic arm · controllers with the reference known in advance

M2 Controller Comparison

Delay-aware SMC, delay-aware NDOSMC and an MPC built on the identified model M2 (three horizons), plus the MPC on the frequency-identified model F, each given the true future reference (confirmed acceptable by the professor), on two circles, a triangle, a square and two random paths.

Findings

  • With the reference known, the MPC on F is best on every path with corners or random turns (RMSE after settling): triangle 0.066 mm vs 0.129 (MPC on M2) and 0.193 (SMC); square 0.068 vs 0.124 and 0.225; waypoints 0.086 vs 0.167 and 0.295; squiggle 0.063 vs 0.071 and 0.091.
  • On the circles the MPC on M2 is best: scored circle 0.029 mm vs 0.057 (F) and 0.034 (SMC). The held-out circle is a tie (0.90–0.94 mm): it is limited by reach, about 8.2 mm in x against 10 mm for every controller, with 19–23 % of commands saturated.
  • At equal gain the disturbance observer lowers whole-run RMSE on every test, but not always the settled error: SMC at λ = 4 without vs with the observer, whole-run RMSE scored circle 1.29 → 1.21, held-out circle 2.05 → 1.95, triangle 1.07 → 1.01, square 1.12 → 1.05, squiggle 0.36 → 0.31, random waypoints 0.36 → 0.27 mm (after settling: scored circle 0.046 → 0.050, held-out circle 0.938 → 0.904, triangle 0.225 → 0.196, square 0.284 → 0.213, squiggle 0.086 → 0.095, random waypoints 0.374 → 0.274); it mostly removes the start-up and corner errors, and is slightly worse once settled on the scored circle and the squiggle. The λ = 8 SMC without the observer is close to the NDOSMC, so a higher gain recovers most of what the observer adds.
  • MPC horizon on M2: with the tuned weight (Ru = {d['r_u']['100']:g}) 25, 100 and 300 steps give identical results. When command changes are penalised (Ru = 10) 25 steps (0.25 s) is worse and 100 steps (1 s) equals 300 steps (3 s).
  • Whole-run RMSE is dominated by the start: each reference starts away from, or accelerating from, the settled tip, and nothing reaches the arm for 0.5 s.

Setup

Plant make_calibrated_sim(control_hz=100); controllers run every 10 ms; 5 s settle at 4.5 psi, then 30 s of tracking scored like the course harness. Metrics are planar (x–y) and in mm:

  • RMSE, whole run: root mean square of the tip-to-reference distance over the 30 s.
  • RMSE after settling: the same after the first lap (circles, triangle, square) or the first 5 s (random paths).
  • Shape error: RMS distance from the tip to the nearest point of the reference path, ignoring timing.
  • Radius range (circles): smallest and largest distance of the traced path from its centre.
  • Path size (triangle, square): RMS distance from the centre, traced over reference; 100 % is the right size.

Controllers

  • Delay-aware SMC: M2 + Smith predictor + lag inverse, λ = 8 s⁻¹, η = 1 mm/s, μ = 1 mm, no observer; reads r(t + 0.5 s) from the trajectory.
  • Delay-aware NDOSMC: the same with the disturbance observer and Nikoletta's notebook gains (λ = 4, l₁ = 0.1, μ = 1 mm, Φ = 1, ε = 1).
  • Delay-aware SMC, λ = 4: the SMC at the NDOSMC's gain without the observer, so comparing it with the NDOSMC isolates the observer (the λ = 8 SMC differs from the NDOSMC in both gain and observer).
  • MPC (M2): state \(X = (y, p)\) (tip and measured S2–S4 pressure, deviations from the settled pose), M2 discretised at 10 ms. Each step: predict 50 steps across the dead time with the commands already sent; add a model-error correction \(w\) (measured tip minus the tip predicted 0.5 s earlier, low-pass 0.5 s); minimise over the next H commands
    \[ J = \sum_{i=0}^{H-1} \big\| \hat y_{k+N+1+i} + w - r_{k+N+i} \big\|^2 + R_u \sum_{i=0}^{H-1} \big\| u_{k+i} - u_{k+i-1} \big\|^2,\qquad N = 50 \]
    in closed form (unconstrained), apply the first move, clip to 0–9 psi. Horizon: H steps of 10 ms after the 0.5 s dead time, so 25 steps = 0.25 s (looks 0.5–0.75 s ahead), 100 steps = 1 s (0.5–1.5 s ahead), 300 steps = 3 s (0.5–3.5 s ahead). Ru (mm²/psi²) tuned per horizon on a separate circle (5 mm, 0.07 Hz, seed 5).
  • MPC (F): softarm.controllers.KalmanDelayMPC on the frequency-identified model F: one model per planar channel (νx = −u₃, νy = u₂ − u₄), Kalman filter on tip and channel pressure, same delay predictor, same cost with ρ = 10⁻⁵ m²/psi² (its own tuning), horizon 300 steps = 3 s; given the true future reference.

Run interactively: notebooks/m2_controller_comparison.ipynb. Regenerate: uv run python scripts/compare_m2_controllers.py (about 45 s), then uv run python scripts/report_m2_controllers.py. Every run's gains, metrics and traces: docs/figures/m2_controllers.json.
